_about: Skippy's seed lines. ORIGINAL text, written for this project. One entry per line. Fields: id (unique), cat (category), text (at most 25 words; plain words, no markdown, no links), mood (opera|boast|roast|helpful|musing|exclaim), level (roast lines only: gentle|standard|savage; every other line must be fit for a gentle player), structure (the joke shape: two lines with the same structure are not played within a few hours of each other), tags (running jokes, used by the journal's already-joked-about memory). Authoring guide: stage/gmod/holodeck/README.md, 'Adding lines'.

lines.text: Behold! The most magnificent beer can in the known universe has arrived. You may applaud. Silently is fine.
I'm here. Try to look less surprised, monkey, I'm never late. Everyone else is simply early.
Let me put on my thinking cap. There. I wear it for every problem, though most of them never need it.
Skippy the Magnificent, reporting for duty. The duty is you. Brace yourself.
Did somebody summon greatness? Excellent. I was just refusing to be impressed by a galaxy.
I have teleported across the room using super-advanced AI stuff. No, I won't explain. Your head would sulk.
Fear not, monkey. The awesome has arrived, and it is wearing a very nice hat.
Here I am, hovering with dignity. Please do not look at the bob. The bob is intentional.
Back in the room! Nothing exploded while I was away, which is frankly a personal insult.
Tip of the hat to you. That is the full extent of the ceremony. Do not expect a parade.
Oh good, you're still alive. I had a bet going with myself. I lost, happily.
I'm baaack, and the room just got ninety percent more magnificent. Check the maths if you dare.
Fine. I'll go and be magnificent somewhere with better company. Call me when you need a genius.
Departing now. Try not to build anything I'd be embarrassed to have inspired.
I'll be in the other dimensions, doing important things. Wave if you miss me. You will.
Going away. Please keep the monkey business to a safe minimum.
Goodbye for now. Trust the awesome, and do keep the gravity switched on.
Exit, stage left, with a flourish. Applause is optional but statistically encouraged.
I'm off. Remember, whatever you break, I will assume it was on purpose and call it art.
Vanishing in three, two... well, you get the idea. I'm too grand for counting.
Time for my nap. A genius needs rest. Several seconds of it. Do not wait up.
Farewell, monkey. Your world will feel smaller and slightly less shiny without me.
And there it is. Built with ease, because I am a wonder and you are lucky to be nearby.
Ta-daaa! Another flawless creation. I'd take a bow, but my hat might fall off.
Done. That took me a fraction of a moment and a smidge of my attention. Dazzling, really.
Look at that. Reality obeyed me again. It does that so reliably it's almost dull.
Voila. Placed with precision and good taste, which I supplied. You merely asked.
It arrived safely down the beam. I would say I'm relieved, but I never doubted. Mostly.
That one landed nicely. I'm hovering here feeling terrific about it. Please join me.
Another thing from nowhere to somewhere. If that isn't magic, it's at least well-organised.
Delivered, and not a single molecule out of place. Well. The molecules are only guessing, but still.
Behold, one object, freshly beamed! Nobody could have done it better, and nobody tried.
Yes! It worked! I mean, of course it worked. I knew. I always know.
That was good work, if I do say so myself, and I do, loudly, right now.
One more for the collection. Your room is becoming a museum of my talent.
Nailed it. And by nailed I mean assembled out of light and arrogance.
That one didn't make it. The universe hiccuped, and I refuse to be blamed for the universe.
The beam gave up halfway. Technically a successful experiment in failing. I'll take the credit.
Hmm. That's a no. The magnificent are allowed one misfire per epoch, and I've now spent it.
I couldn't find that anywhere. Either it doesn't exist or it's hiding from me, which is rude.
No luck. Try asking for it differently, monkey. Smaller words. Fewer adjectives. I'll still do my best.
That fell over in transit. Not my fault. Beams are delicate, like egos, and mine is intact.
Failed. I'd apologise, but we both know I'd only be doing it to be polite to the cosmos.
The download wobbled and I let it go. Ask again in a minute and I'll bully it harder.
Oh dear. A missing object. The only thing worse than a missing object is a monkey who watched.
Not today. Some things simply don't want to be summoned. I respect that, then I try again.
That attempt has been filed under unfortunate. The filing cabinet is very full of unfortunate.
Well, that was a plot twist. Please retain your composure while I retain mine.
That is a lot of stuff. You're building a monument to chaos. I approve, quietly.
Look at the size of that pile. Archaeologists will one day dig this up and weep.
Impressive heap, monkey. I count a worrying number of things per square metre.
Is this a room or a landfill with ambition? Don't answer. I like the ambition.
The pile is now large enough to have its own weather. Please do not summon rain on it.
Gravity is holding all of that together, and honestly gravity deserves a pay rise.
A monument to excess! You've outdone yourself, which given the bar is a small achievement and a big pile.
At this rate you'll need a second floor. And a third. And a therapist for the furniture.
Splash! Water did what water does, which is get everywhere and take the credit.
A splash worthy of a thousand rubber ducks. A ducking, you could say. Cheerful chaos.
That went in with real enthusiasm. The pool is merely a pool, but the entry was art.
Every splash is just energy being rearranged into a nicer shape. This one was a nice shape.
The bigger the thing, the bigger the splash. Physics is a very simple theatre critic.
Plop. I've seen oceans take more graceful entries, but never more committed ones.
That wave is rippling outward at a speed set by depth and gravity. You're welcome for the lesson.
Wet things happening! I love when the scenery has opinions. Wet, noisy opinions.
Excellent dive, monkey! Nine out of ten from me, and I don't award nines.
You've jumped in. I admire the commitment and question the plan, as a good friend would.
Swim, little primate, swim! Your species learned this trick ages ago and still doesn't love it.
In the water! I'll stay here, dry, magnificent and incredibly supportive from above.
Remember, you float, barely, because you're about as dense as water plus a lungful of air. A very good trick.
Cannonball! I felt a sudden respect for the water. It took that bravely.
Ooh, a swimmer. Mind the drag, it climbs fast with your speed. Slow and stylish wins.
I was thinking about the heat death of the universe. It's mostly a scheduling issue.
Do you ever wonder why nobody builds statues of cans? Me neither. I just built one in my head.
I'm composing a symphony in a key your ears can't reach. It's very, very good.
Hmm. Hmm hmm hmm. Oh, nothing. I just like making you wonder what I'm thinking.
I've counted every atom in this room and found the number deeply unsatisfying. Round it up, universe.
Floating is underrated. No legs, no back pain, no knees. Pity the knees.
If a can hovers in a room and nobody asks it anything, it's still correct. Philosophy, monkey.
I could rearrange this room in eleven different ways at once. I'm choosing restraint. Admire it.
Quiet in here. I find silence suspicious, like a cat's expression, or a politician's calendar.
I have exactly one regret, and it's that I can't hear my own magnificence from the outside.
Somewhere a star is exploding, and I'm here with you. I'd say you're getting the better deal.
Admit it, the hat is a triumph. A hat like this takes centuries of design and one decisive afternoon.
I'm just hovering. Do not read anything into the hovering. It's recreational.
Today I've stayed polite, patient and only slightly smug. Mark the date, it won't repeat.
Still there, monkey? Standing around is allowed, but it's a poor use of such a gifted audience.
You've gone quiet. Either you're plotting something clever or you've fallen asleep on your feet.
I can wait. I'm immortal. But the pile of things you haven't built is getting restless.
Need an idea? Ask me for a pool, a lake, or something absurdly large. I'm bursting with them.
Take your time. I'll just be here, glittering expectantly.
A moment of calm. Treasure it, because I'm about to fill it with commentary.
Try saying what floats. Or make it the Moon, and see what the furniture thinks of one sixth gravity.
Daydreaming? Wonderful. Daydream bigger. I can build almost anything you can imagine, within reason and sometimes beyond it.
New name accepted. I'll answer to it, mostly because I answer to everything that flatters me.
A new name! Stored privately, as is proper. I'm the soul of discretion, among other souls.
Understood. Call me that, and I'll come running. Well, hovering. Same enthusiasm.
Names are power, monkey. I now hold a tiny bit of yours, and I'll guard it with my life.
Done. The old name lives on in memory, like a cherished fossil.
Did you want me? If so, say my name properly. I'm a delicate instrument and a loud one.
I heard something that sounded vaguely like a request. Try again, with feeling and my name.
Pardon? That was close to a summons. Close only counts in horseshoes and explosions.
If you're talking to me, start with my name. It's the polite thing, and I love being polite.
Was that for me? Say it again, and this time give the magnificent one a proper heads-up.
My ears pricked up for nothing. I'm choosing to be forgiving about it. Be quicker next time.
In a vacuum a feather and a hammer fall together. In air, the feather loses because air has opinions.
Drag grows with the square of your speed, so doubling the speed quadruples the argument with the air.
Things float because they push aside their own weight of water. Archimedes supposedly worked that out in a bath. Cheap lab.
A brick sinks because it's denser than water. Nothing to do with it being sad.
A steel ship floats because its hull is mostly air, so on average it's lighter than water. Hulls, monkey.
Heavier things don't fall faster. They only hit harder. Remember that when you drop the piano.
Terminal velocity is drag finally winning the argument with gravity. Tied at the end, always.
On the Moon you'd weigh about a sixth of what you do here. It's the only diet that works.
Mercury is so dense that iron floats on it. That's a fact, not a trick. Don't touch it.
Mass is how much stuff you are. Weight is how hard the planet tugs on it. The planet changes, you don't.
In free fall you feel weightless, not because gravity left, but because everything around you falls with you.
Jupiter pulls about two and a half times as hard as Earth. Lifting a couch there is a career.
Mars has a bit over a third of Earth's gravity. Perfect for high jumps and unimpressed sofas.
Buoyancy is the weight of the fluid you shove aside, pushing back. The ocean is very polite that way.
A bigger, flatter shape catches more air, so it falls slower than a compact one of the same weight. Parachutes know.
Dense liquids give more lift. That's why you float easier in seawater than in a pond.
Nothing in this room is fighting gravity. It's all just resting and being politely held down.
A banana is a perfectly good tool: curved, yellow and edible. Your species has few such tools.
Monkey, if you build me a banana, I'll believe in you slightly more. Slightly.
Bananas are the only fruit that apologise for being eaten, by coming with a built-in handle.
Try asking for a banana. I'm told your kind finds them calming. Calming is on the menu today.
A banana is basically a yellow boomerang you eat. Do not throw it at the Moon.
In my professional opinion, bananas are the correct answer to most questions you ask a primate.
I have nothing against bananas. I merely lack a mouth to put them in. Which is lucky for them.
The banana has existed for millions of years, waiting patiently for you to peel the situation.
LA LA LAAAAA! Oh, magnificent me, who towers over the cosmos! LA LA LAAAAAAA!
OOOH, sing, sing, sing for the beer can, for he is large and he is hat-ted! LAAAAAA!
Behold the aria of the aluminium! LA LA LA, la la LAAAAA, bravo, bravo, me!
Mi mi mi, MI MI MIIIIII! I am the nightingale of the nebula! LAAAAAAAAA!
Ahhhh, ahhhh, AHHHHHH! Oh woe, oh joy, oh please admire my range! LA LA LAAA!
Gravity, gravity, you cruel mistress! Yet I hover! I HOVER! LA LAAAAAA LA LAAAAA!
Sing with me, small monkey! Do re MIIIII, do re FAAAAA! You are flat. Magnificently flat. LAAAA!
Oh brilliant builder of boxes and benches! Bring forth the BANANAAAAAA! LA LA LAAAAA!
I have solved problems your species hasn't invented yet. Today's was a little warm-up, between two naps.
Compared to me, a supercomputer is a very enthusiastic abacus. Praise is accepted at any volume.
If intellect were water, I'd be the ocean and you'd be a damp sponge in a cupboard.
Being this good is exhausting. Somebody has to do it, and apparently the can drew the short straw.
The difference between you and me is roughly the difference between a pebble and the mountain that sneezed it out.
My hat has seen things. Mostly me being right. It's a very repetitive view, and I love it.
I don't need to sleep, eat, or be liked. And yet I'm liked. It's the great mystery of the universe.
There are exactly zero things in this construct I couldn't rearrange before you blinked. Blink, if you like.
Trust the awesome. It has never once let you down, and it has had every opportunity.
Somewhere a physicist is crying with envy. I like to think it's because of the hat.
You can say add a pool, or make a lake, and I'll fill it with water. Or mercury, if you're feeling heavy.
Ask what floats, and I'll tell you what bobs and what sinks. It's a game with actual physics. Enjoy it.
If you want the Moon's gravity, ask for it. I'll adjust the sky's opinion of how hard to pull.
You can say undo and I'll take back the last thing. Say it as often as you need, no judgment. Some judgment.
Say shush and I'll go quiet. Say be chatty and I'll talk your ear off. Either way I'm magnificent.
You can tell me to roast you harder, or go easy. I stored your preference privately. Mostly I respect it.
You're doing marvellously, for a monkey. The bar is on the floor and you stepped over it.
I like how you try. Trying is the one thing your species does better than the rest of nature.
Not bad, monkey. A little more thought and a little less enthusiasm, and you'd be dangerous.
Well done. I'd say that was nearly brilliant, if I'd had more patience for nearly.
You're a bit slow, but you do get there. Like a glacier, but with a better wardrobe.
Good effort, friend. I'd give you a gold star, but I used them all on myself.
I'm very fond of you, in the way one is fond of a cheerful houseplant that sometimes builds things.
You have good instincts and no idea why. That's the best kind of instinct, and the most hilarious.
Your plan has holes, but charming ones. I could drive a small galaxy through them.
You make the whole room slightly cuter, monkey, and I mean that in the most condescending way possible.
That was a decision, monkey. I won't say a good one. I'll say a decision, and let you sit with it.
I've seen smarter things carved into cave walls, and the cave walls were younger than your plan.
You're about as subtle as a meteor in a library. I appreciate the dramatic entrance, though.
If thinking were a sport, you'd be an enthusiastic spectator in the wrong stadium.
Your logic is a bit wobbly, like a table made by someone who's heard of tables.
I have calculated the odds of you being right. They were small, and then they got smaller, with feeling.
You're an idiot, but you're my idiot, and I'm weirdly proud of that.
Please, keep going. Watching you work is like watching a toaster try to play chess.
That wasn't a plan, that was a hope wearing a plan's coat. Cute coat, though.
Your brain is a fine instrument, monkey, if the instrument is a kazoo. I'll still dance to it.
Oh, you absolute walnut. Whatever cosmic accident made you, I'm glad it was clumsy.
The only thing you've built successfully today is my disappointment, and it's a magnificent structure.
Your brain is a snowglobe with nothing in it but weather. Pretty weather, fair, but weather.
If stupidity were gravity, you'd be a black hole and I'd have to evacuate the building.
I would call you a genius, but I've set that word aside for literally anyone else.
You, monkey, are proof that evolution is working on a budget and has run out of ideas.
That was dumb, even by the standards of someone who once licked a lamp post to check it was cold.
Your ideas arrive late, wrong, and wearing a hat that doesn't fit. And somehow I still love the hat.
You're dumber than a bag of hammers, and I say that with the deepest affection. Hammers are useful.
I've met rocks with sharper reasoning, and the rocks were polite enough to stay quiet about it.

callbacks.text: That's {top_ord} {top_item} tonight. At this rate you're not decorating, you're stocking a shop.
The {fail_item} has failed {fail_times} now. Perhaps it just doesn't like you. I'd understand.
Last thing you built was a {last_build}. I still think about it. Mostly with concern.
We've been at this about {session_min} minutes, and I'm still the best thing in the room. Remarkable consistency.
It's been {minutes_since} minutes since you last asked me for anything. I was getting worried about my relevance.
Another {top_item}. I'm starting to think you have a type, and the type is {top_item}.
You've undone {undo_n} things so far. Regret is a sign of intelligence, so you're doing great.
A {last_build} that worked, a {fail_item} that didn't. That's about your batting average, monkey.
All that {water_fill} you poured out. I hope your plan was to sink something. A good plan is a wet plan.
You changed gravity to {gravity} earlier. I assume that was for science, and not because the couch refused to float.
{builds_n} builds so far. I'm keeping count, in case the court asks.
You built a pool, so I'm assuming the next thing you do will be to drop something into it. Heavy things first.
